study.title: Proverbs 1 The call to wisdom and the choice between two paths
study.overview: Proverbs 1 presents the purpose of the book: to teach practical wisdom, moral discipline, justice and discernment. The chapter contrasts two paths. On the one hand, the invitation of sinners to the rogue violence and profit, which ends in ruin. On the other hand, the call of wisdom, which is public, insistent and offered to all, but also requires obedient response. The climax is in the contrast between rejecting instruction and inhabiting safely when listening to it.

outline.title: Purpose of book and foundation of knowledge
outline.explanation: The initial verses explain that the proverbs aim to form character: giving prudence, justice, judgment and discernment. Wisdom here is not just information, but the ability to live straightly. The fear of the Lord appears as the principle of knowledge, in contrast to the posture of fools, who despise instruction.

outline.title: The warning against bad companies and greed
outline.explanation: The father directs the son not to follow sinners who promise easy gain through violence and plunder. The text shows that who ambushes ambushes for others is actually preparing their own destruction. Greed is portrayed as a self-destructive path, because unjust profit ends up taking the life of the seeker.

outline.title: Wisdom publicly cries
outline.explanation: Wisdom is personified as someone who screams in the streets and squares, reaching everyone. She confronts the simple, scoffers and madmen, calling to repentance. The desired answer is to listen to rebuke and receive instruction rather than resist it.

outline.title: Consequences of rejection and security for those who listen
outline.explanation: Whoever repeatedly rejects the counsel of wisdom will reap the fruit of his own ways when calamity comes. The chapter ends with a promise: whoever hears wisdom will dwell in safety and without fear of evil. Moral choice therefore has real and inevitable consequences.

study.context: The chapter works as a programmatic opening of the book, presenting its pedagogical and moral objective. The notes provided highlight that biblical wisdom is practical and ethical, focused on correct choices, and that the fear of the Lord is central. There are no additional historical details in the given notes other than the association of the book to Solomon.
study.theology: Theologically, Proverbs 1 teaches that wisdom begins with reverent submission to God. True knowledge is not neutral: it includes justice, prudence, and moral discipline. The chapter also affirms human responsibility in the face of divine instruction. Wisdom is presented as a public and insistent call, but persistent refusal hardens the heart and brings judgment. At the same time, there is grace in the invitation: listening to wisdom leads to safety, not because of the absence of dangers, but by the protection of God and by the direction of an upright life.

scholarViews.insight: Wisdom is practical knowledge that involves ethical choices; learning it requires discipline and opposition to natural sinful tendencies.
The fear of the Lord is placed as the principle of knowledge, and honoring God must come before any moral formation.
The hearing of wisdom results in inhabiting in safety, with full tranquility before evil, in contrast to those who reject the counsel.

questions: How have I treated biblical wisdom: how useful information or as a direction for concrete decisions?
Which voices around me are inviting me to shortcuts, easy earnings or unfair attitudes?
Has my reaction to God's reproof been of resistance or obedient repentance?
study.practice: This week, read Proverbs 1 in two passages: first 1:1-7 and then 1:8-33. When reading, identify an area where you have been looking for a shortcut or have listened to wrong influences. Then do a concrete action of obedience: cut an influence, ask godly counsel to a mature person in the faith and set aside daily time to ask God for a teachable heart. The application of the chapter is not only to admire the wisdom, but to choose the path of it.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided do not explain all verses individually, so some connections between parts of the text and theological application are syntheses made from the chapter itself. It was also not possible to confirm, only with the notes given, detailed historical data on authorship, dates or circumstances of composition beyond the traditional assignment to Solomon.
